history.origins: Marafon-Beccaccino is characteristic of the Italian province of Romagna. It is a four-player partnership game based on Tressette with the addition of a trump suit. The first printed reference to Beccaccino appears in 1971 in Libero Ercolani's Vocabolario romagnolo-italiano (Ravenna). Earlier the game was known as "tri sett cun el taj" (Tressette with cutting). The composite name Marafon-Beccaccino was coined in Alteo Dolcini's Il Principe di Romagna (Imola, 1975), which codified official rules.

history.cultural: The signature card game of Romagna.
history.evolution: Tressette with trumps. Parent game of Trionfino.

rules.objective: Reach 41 points first with your partner; Maraffa and last-trick bonuses apply.
rules.gameplay: Follow suit. Trump if void. 3-2-A ranking. Maraffa: Declare if holding A+2+3 trumps = 3 bonus pts. Communication: Busso (knock), Striscio (indicate 2), Tiro (indicate A). Total 11 pts/hand + Maraffa.

strategy.basic: Choose trump in longest/strongest suit. Declare Maraffa when eligible.
strategy.intermediate: Use legal signals to coordinate with partner.
strategy.advanced: Card counting across 10-trick hands. Manage the endgame for last-trick bonus.
tips: Last trick is worth fighting for.
